cfg.m0FollowupAnswer: Marco double-books the 6pm slot and members show up to a class that is already full.

answers.m2: Marco walked me through last Tuesday: two members arrived for the 18:00 class he had already filled. He refunded one at the front desk and comped the other a personal training session.
answers.m3: My friend Priya, who runs a yoga studio, told me last month she started capping sign-ups in a shared spreadsheet after a similar double-booking during a holiday rush.
answers.m4: Owen, a barber who takes walk-ins, keeps a paper appointment book by the chair. For him the pain is no-shows, the overbooking part is fine.
answers.m5: Marco uses a shared Google Calendar for the class roster, but it doesn't stop two people from claiming the same slot if they both edit it around the same time.
answers.m6: "I hate turning people away at the door," he said after the Tuesday one.
answers.m7: Jordan runs one-on-one training sessions only, no group classes. Double-booking never happens to him because every slot has exactly one client.
